title: V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio+axum, http.rs deleted
description:
## Outcome
vault-node serves /sign + /events via axum on tokio (one port, fully async), with http.rs deleted. Behavior-neutral for what the coordinator consumes. This async base is the prerequisite for the node channel (V0-8a) and every timer-driven milestone after it (V0-8b Hold-expiry combine, V0-4 duress T).

## Why this exists
The hand-rolled synchronous HTTP server (crates/vault-node/src/http.rs) is one sequential serve loop: a stalled client head-of-line-blocks /sign for up to 10s, and it cannot host the peer-facing /channel route or async timers. Migrating while the surface is two routes is far cheaper than after V0-8a/V0-8b/V0-4 pile onto the sync shape (2026-07-16 eng review).

## Verification (ship gate)
nix develop -c cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; demo first-light exits 0. http.rs no longer exists. The new HTTP-level regression tests lock the axum edge contract, and the sign-path atomicity + no-cancel tests prove the concurrency model.

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
The whole node runs from tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death. "State on disk" never means durable; nothing this task writes needs to survive a reboot.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio + axum — behavior-neutral where it counts, http.rs deleted

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- This is a **mechanical migration**. It exists so the next task (V0-8a, the
  node channel) lands on an async base as a small, security-only diff.
  Decision record (2026-07-16 eng review): the node goes **fully async**
  (tokio + axum), all surfaces on **one port**, because V0-8a adds a
  peer-facing route and V0-8b/V0-4 add timers (Hold-expiry, duress T).
  Deployment context (ADR-0007, informs no code here but explains the state
  model): the whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk** — reboot = bare machine
  = node death. So "state on disk" never means durable; nothing this task
  writes needs to survive a reboot.

## Problem description
`crates/vault-node/src/http.rs` is a hand-rolled synchronous HTTP/1.1 server —
one sequential serve loop, one request at a time. It was right when `/sign` was
the only route; it is wrong as the base for the channel (head-of-line blocking:
a stalled client holds the loop up to 10s) and for the timer-driven milestones
after it. Replace it with axum on tokio.

**Compatibility contract (be precise about what "behavior-neutral" means):**
- **Byte-compatible** for what the coordinator consumes: `POST /sign` → 200
  with the exact signed/pending/refusal JSON; 400 with `{"error": detail}` on
  an undecodable body (`BadRequest` stays 400, never a refusal). `GET /events`
  / `/events?since=<cursor>` → same JSON; absent/unparseable `since` reads 0.
- **Edge statuses adopt axum's standard answers** (oversized body may be 413,
  wrong method 405, unknown route 404 with axum's body, query strings routed by
  path). Do NOT replicate the hand-rolled server's quirks — instead the
  regression tests below CAPTURE the new edge contract so it is explicit and
  locked from now on.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)
1. **Add deps**: `tokio` (rt-multi-thread, macros, time, net) and `axum` to
   vault-node. Workspace-pin versions; `Cargo.lock` changes accordingly.
   Nothing else — no tower-http, no tracing stack, no reqwest (V0-8a adds it).
2. **Port routes to axum** per the compatibility contract above. Body limit
   stays 1 MiB (`DefaultBodyLimit`). Add a request-timeout layer for handler
   execution. A client that stalls mid-headers no longer wedges anything (each
   connection is its own task — that is the point of the migration); a
   socket-level header-read deadline is v1 hardening, NOT this task.
3. **Sign-path atomicity (critical).** Today the sequential serve loop gives
   `handle_sign` end-to-end atomicity for free: its check-then-update sequences
   over the replay and pending logs (`replay_log`, `pending_log` at
   lib.rs:134-138) never interleave. Under axum, requests are concurrent.
   Preserve the CURRENT semantics: **one sign-path `Mutex`** serializing the
   whole `handle_sign` call — do NOT convert the two `RefCell`s to independent
   `Mutex`es (interleaved check/update between two concurrent identical
   requests would corrupt replay semantics). Document at the lock: **`/sign` is
   serialized BY DESIGN** — concurrency buys ISOLATION of `/sign` from
   `/events`/`/channel`, NOT sign-vs-sign throughput; two `/sign` requests
   still run one-at-a-time and that is correct. Run the (synchronous,
   CPU-bearing) `handle_sign` body inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so
   descriptor scans/secp work never stall the runtime. **An accepted sign job
   must NOT be cancelled by a handler timeout** — a half-run sign that mutated
   the replay/pending log then got dropped is a ghost side effect; let accepted
   `/sign` work run to completion (the handler timeout guards connection
   liveness, not the committed sign job). Concretely: wrap the `spawn_blocking`
   JoinHandle in `tokio::time::timeout`; on timeout, drop the response future
   (the client gets a timeout status) but let the blocking task finish and
   commit its verdict. Recovery is by idempotent resubmission — the anti-replay
   log returns the recorded verdict for an identical commitment (DESIGN.md
   "anti-replay log" §, job (1) idempotency).
4. **Delete `http.rs`** — do not keep two HTTP stacks. Its `parse_since` unit
   test moves/adapts to wherever cursor parsing now lives.
5. **`main.rs`** becomes `#[tokio::main]`; serve the one axum app on
   `listen_port`.
6. **Watchtower driver**: `Node::spawn_watchtower`'s interval thread becomes a
   tokio interval task whose tick body runs via `spawn_blocking` (the tick
   calls blocking bitcoind JSON-RPC in `chain.rs`; a slow RPC must never stall
   the async runtime). `chain.rs` itself does NOT need an async rewrite.
7. **`Node` stays as it is** otherwise. Do not restructure its fields or make
   policy code async.

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- All existing unit tests pass unchanged (policy, handle_sign, watchtower,
  replay) — except `http.rs`'s `parse_since` test, which moves with the code.
- **HTTP-level regression tests (NEW — the point of this task):** over a real
  loopback socket against the axum app:
  - `POST /sign` valid body → 200, exact response JSON shape.
  - `POST /sign` garbage → 400 `{"error": ...}`.
  - Oversized body (> 1 MiB) → rejected with the axum-standard status —
    assert the status you get and lock it as the contract; never 500 or hang.
  - `GET /events?since=42` and bare `/events` → cursor semantics unchanged.
  - Unknown route → 404; wrong method → assert-and-lock the axum answer.
- **Concurrency regression:** two identical `/sign` requests submitted
  concurrently → exactly one fresh acceptance path runs; replay/pending logs
  end consistent (no interleaving corruption). (`/sign` serializes against
  `/sign` by design — do NOT assert two signs overlap.)
- **Isolation:** a slow/blocking `/sign` (or a watchtower tick with a slow
  chain backend) does not delay `GET /events` — assert `/events` stays
  responsive while a sign job is in flight. This is what the async migration
  buys; it is NOT sign-vs-sign parallelism. (`/channel` gets the same
  isolation guarantee in V0-8a, where it exists.)
- **No-cancel sign job:** a `/sign` that exceeds the handler timeout returns a
  timeout status to the client, BUT the accepted job completes and commits its
  verdict (replay/pending logs consistent), and an identical resubmission
  returns the recorded verdict — no ghost half-run, no lost sign. (Assert all
  three: client sees timeout, log mutated once, resubmit is idempotent.)
- `nix develop -c cargo run -p vault-cli -- demo first-light` exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, the workspace `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock`
  only. Do NOT add any channel/peer code (V0-8a), do NOT touch the
  coordinator, policy-core, vault-proto, or the demo. Do NOT change any
  request/response JSON schema.
- Target ≤ 700 lines net including the new tests. If materially more, stop
  and simplify.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`, `nix develop -c cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `nix develop -c cargo test --workspace` pass.
- `http.rs` no longer exists; the node serves `/sign` + `/events` via axum
  meeting the compatibility contract, proven by the HTTP-level regression
  tests, including the sign-path atomicity test.
- `demo first-light` exits 0.

---
## Polish notes (bead-polish-loop 2026-07-16)
- **This bead unblocks btc-policy-byf (the node channel) and MUST merge first.** It is a behavior-neutral migration — reviewers should confirm no observable /sign or /events behavior changed except the deliberately-locked axum edge statuses (413/405/404 bodies).
- **Authoritative design source (committed):** the "fully async, one port" decision is docs/DESIGN.md + the 2026-07-16 eng review; tmpfs reboot-death is docs/adr/0007-node-death-on-reboot.md. No ADR schema changes in this task.

title: V0-8a: node-to-node channel (signed envelopes + verified partial exchange)
description:
## Outcome
vault-node gains an authenticated node-to-node channel: per-message signed envelopes (no session) over POST /channel on the existing axum app, plus a verified partial-signature exchange primitive backed by a candidate registry populated by the real /sign path. These are the primitives V0-8b drives to combine + broadcast; this task builds ONLY the channel layer.

## Why this exists
Under Model B the coordinator is a pure relay: nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and broadcast. That requires an authenticated channel that carries signatures and assembly only — never policy — and a way for a node to verify a peer's partial against its OWN recomputed sighash (never blind-merge a peer PSBT). ADR-0012 "The node-to-node channel" + ADR-0013 §4 (manifest) are authoritative.

## Critical security properties (must all hold)
- Channel identity endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key, verified against the immutable manifest — the coordinator cannot mint/impersonate a node.
- Per-message possession proof (envelope signature over a fresh nonce+timestamp) — no session handshake.
- recipient_node_id binds each envelope to its receiver — closes cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future msg_type.
- Signature covers the RAW payload_b64 field (verify BEFORE decode) — identity before payload parsing.
- Partials verified against the expected descriptor pubkey over the node's OWN registered sighash — never blind-merge.
- Signing-oracle prohibition: structurally no channel message can cause the node to sign.

## Non-goals / scope guard
Touch crates/vault-node/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock ONLY. The ONLY /sign-path change is the register_candidate post-verdict funnel. Do NOT build combine/broadcast (V0-8b), duress state machine (V0-4), Tor/mTLS (v1), full manifest provisioning (V0-9), or any session/connection state. Target ~1200-1600 lines incl tests.

## Verification (ship gate)
fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace green; demo first-light exits 0; the two-in-process-nodes E2E exchanges one verified partial THROUGH the real /sign→/channel path (no test-only candidate injection).

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death; a dead node never rejoins the immutable manifest (restore capacity = rotate to a successor vault). No channel state persists.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a: node-to-node channel — identity, signed envelopes, partial-signature exchange

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- **Prerequisite: V0-8a0 (axum migration) is merged.** The node is async
  (tokio + axum, one port, `http.rs` deleted, sign-path Mutex +
  spawn_blocking). Build the channel as routes and tasks on that base. All new
  code is async.
- Read `docs/adr/0012-model-b-spend-and-duress-architecture.md` (**"The
  node-to-node channel"** section — the authoritative security properties) and
  `docs/adr/0013-concrete-protocol-schemas.md` (§4 manifest — the
  channel-identity root). Also `CONTEXT.md` ("Node channel", "Manifest").
- This is the **channel layer only**. It does NOT rework the spend path or the
  coordinator (that is V0-8b). It provides the primitives V0-8b will drive:
  authenticated peer messaging + a verified partial-signature exchange.

## Problem description
Under Model B, nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and
broadcast (the coordinator is a pure relay). This task builds the
**authenticated peer messaging** those nodes use, and the **partial-signature
exchange** primitive — but NOT the combine/broadcast wiring or the spend-path
rework (V0-8b). The channel carries signatures and assembly only, **never
policy**.

Design decisions locked by the 2026-07-16 eng review (do not re-litigate):
- **No session handshake.** Every peer message is a self-authenticating
  **signed envelope** (possession is proven per message — the fresh
  nonce+timestamp IS the challenge). This satisfies ADR-0012's
  challenge-response/possession requirement with no connection state machine.
- **Same port.** Channel messages are a route (`POST /channel`) on the node's
  one axum app. Axum's concurrency removes the head-of-line-blocking that
  motivated a separate port; layered DoS guards handle peer spam.
  **Principle (2026-07-16): no endpoint on a node derives ANY authority from
  network reachability — all authority is cryptographic, rooted in the
  manifest.** The coordinator can reach `/channel` and peers can reach
  `/sign`; both gain nothing (envelopes need an endorsed channel key; sign
  requests need user/coordinator signatures). Firewalls are hygiene, never a
  trust boundary.
- **Node-local types.** The envelope types live in `vault-node` — the
  coordinator never parses channel messages (V0-8b is also node-side).
- **Reboot survival is a NON-goal.** The whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk**
  (ADR-0007): reboot = bare machine = **permanent node death** (a dead node
  never rejoins the immutable manifest; restoring capacity means rotating to a
  successor vault, not resurrecting the node). No channel state (nonce cache,
  partial store, candidates) needs to persist.
  Derivation determinism (below) exists so the setup-time endorsement matches
  the runtime key — not to survive reboots.
- **Outbound HTTP client = `reqwest`** (user decision 2026-07-16): V0-8b/V0-4
  and v1 (SOCKS/Tor) reuse it.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)

### 1. Channel identity (ADR-0012)
Each node has a **RAM-only channel keypair**, derived **deterministically**
from the node's key material:
`channel_seckey = tagged_hash("btc-policy/channel-key/v0", node_seckey)`
(reduce mod n to a valid secp scalar, retry-increment on the negligible
invalid case; write the tag string once as a const). Never persisted; derived
at startup. Deterministic so the setup-time endorsement and the runtime key
always agree; must differ from the signing key. (V0-9 swaps the seed input to
wskdf without changing the shape.)

The channel pubkey is **endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key** over a
domain-separated structure `(wallet_id, manifest_hash, node_id,
channel_pubkey, protocol_version, transport_endpoints)`. A node accepts a
peer's channel identity **only** if the endorsement verifies against a signing
pubkey bound to that `node_id` in the (immutable) manifest for this vault.
The coordinator cannot mint or impersonate a node.

### 2. Manifest (minimal but real — full provisioning is V0-9)
- `ConfigFile` gains: `node_id` (this node), and `peers` — a list of
  `{ node_id, endpoint, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey, channel_endorsement }`.
  **`channel_pubkey` is REQUIRED** (manifest hashing and envelope verification
  both need it — codex fix 2026-07-16). At startup assert the node_ids form an
  **exact `0..n-1` bijection** with the descriptor's canonical node keys
  (§1 ordering); a gap, dup, or out-of-range id is a fatal config error.
- **Two-pass construction (no hash cycle):** the canonical manifest is the
  endorsement-FREE structure
  `(wallet_id, nodes[node_id, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey,
  transport_endpoints] ordered by node_id, protocol_version)` —
  **`channel_pubkey` IS in the hashed structure** (deterministic, so known at
  setup before endorsements; the manifest exists to pin channel identity).
  `manifest_hash` = tagged SHA-256 over its canonical serialization;
  endorsements are computed OVER that hash and distributed alongside, never
  inside it (ADR-0013 §4). **This v0 `manifest_hash` is PROVISIONAL:** V0-9
  defines the final canonical serialization of the full §4 struct (adding
  vault_descriptor, coordinator_auth_pubkey, t/n, allowlist,
  escape_descriptor) and all endorsements re-derive then — no
  hash continuity is promised before the provisioning ceremony.
- **Startup invariants (assert, fail to start otherwise):** this node's own
  signing pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; every manifest signing
  pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; `node_id` ↔ descriptor-key
  mapping is total and unambiguous (this mapping is also what "expected
  descriptor pubkey for signer X" below means).

### 3. Signed envelopes = peer authentication (the wire contract — exact)
Every channel message is one JSON envelope:
`{ msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
   recipient_node_id, payload_b64, nonce, timestamp, channel_sig }`
- **Crypto:** secp256k1 ECDSA; 33-byte compressed pubkeys; DER signatures
  (consistent with the node's existing signing stack).
- **Signature preimage:** tagged SHA-256 (`"btc-policy/channel-envelope/v0"`)
  over a **canonical length-prefixed byte serialization** of
  `(msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
  recipient_node_id, payload_b64_bytes, nonce, timestamp)` — fixed field
  order, u32-LE length prefix per field, u64-LE for numeric fields. **Sign the
  raw ASCII bytes of the `payload_b64` field, NOT the decoded payload**
  (codex-review fix 2026-07-16: decoding before signature verification is
  forbidden — "identity before payload parsing" — so the signature must cover
  the un-decoded base64 field; the node verifies the envelope, THEN
  base64-decodes `payload_b64`). NOT over serialized JSON.
- **`protocol_version`** is in the envelope AND the preimage; a node rejects
  any envelope whose `protocol_version` ≠ the manifest-pinned version (the
  version lives on the envelope, not the payload; ADR-0013 §4's `BaseManifest`
  pins it). **v0 constant: `protocol_version = 0`** — the minimal in-memory
  manifest sets it to `0` and the node compares against that; define it as a
  named const (`PROTOCOL_VERSION_V0 = 0`), not a magic literal. (V0-9's real
  provisioning carries the same field forward.)
- **`recipient_node_id`** binds the envelope to its intended receiver: a node
  rejects any envelope whose `recipient_node_id` ≠ its own `node_id`. Closes
  cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future `msg_type` (a directed
  message a peer replays to a different node fails the bind), so replay-safety
  never rests on idempotency alone.
- **`payload_b64` is opaque:** base64 of canonical payload bytes, decoded only
  AFTER the envelope authenticates.
- `timestamp`: u64 unix seconds; `nonce`: 16 random bytes, hex.
- **Freshness window (decided 2026-07-16):** accept
  `timestamp ∈ [now − 300s, now + 60s]` — 5 min past tolerance (v1 Tor
  latency + retries + skew), 60s future (skew only). Two `const`s with the
  rationale in a comment, NOT config (hygiene knob, not a ceremony knob — the
  window is hygiene, not safety: every planned msg_type is recipient-bound +
  idempotent). **Nonce-cache prune keys on the envelope's `timestamp`, not
  receipt time** (Fable-review fix 2026-07-16): retain a nonce until
  `timestamp < now − 300` — pruning a future-stamped envelope by receipt time
  would reopen a ~60s replay window. Nodes never exchange or negotiate time —
  no inter-node time protocol, ever (attacker-influenceable input to a hygiene
  mechanism); hosts run NTP (v1 deployment guidance). Use a **monotonic
  high-water mark** for `now` in both the freshness test and the nonce prune
  (never let `now` go backwards) — a backwards NTP step would otherwise let
  pruned nonces re-enter the window with an empty cache. **Count freshness
  rejections per peer** and surface them (an alert/liveness signal) — a node
  whose clock runs >60s fast is silently ejected from the combine set
  otherwise.
- **Receiver verification order:** `protocol_version` = manifest's →
  **`wallet_id` = my vault's AND `manifest_hash` = mine** (explicit
  local-vault equality — codex fix 2026-07-16: the endorsement domain
  separator catches cross-vault indirectly, but a direct equality check is
  cleaner and independently testable) → `recipient_node_id` = my `node_id` →
  sender_node_id in manifest → endorsement valid → `channel_sig` valid over the
  recomputed preimage → `timestamp` within the freshness window → `nonce`
  unseen → only then base64-decode `payload_b64` and dispatch on `msg_type`.
- `msg_type` exists so V0-8b (combine coordination) and V0-4 (duress
  propagation) add message types without a wire break; this task implements
  exactly one: `partial`. **Every registered `msg_type` MUST be recipient-bound
  (via `recipient_node_id`) AND idempotent — each `msg_type` must define an
  explicit idempotency key and pass a duplicate-delivery test before it is
  registered for dispatch** (both-model fix 2026-07-16: "assert idempotent"
  can't enforce semantics, so make it a concrete gate — a type without a
  declared idempotency key + passing dup-delivery test does not ship). For
  `partial` the idempotency key is `(commitment_id, input, signer)` and
  re-delivery re-stores the already-verified partial (a no-op); the nonce
  check is hygiene on top.

### 4. Candidate registry (the seam that makes verification possible)
`/channel` must verify partials against this node's OWN canonical view — which
today dies as a local variable inside `handle_sign`. Add a
`register_candidate(...)` call on `handle_sign`'s **verdict paths** (both the
early-return `Pending` and the signed-response path). **A small, behavior-
preserving control-flow refactor of `handle_sign` is permitted** for this —
"exactly one call site" is not required and cannot cover both a Pending
early-return and a signed return while excluding refusals; a single
post-verdict funnel (`register on Pending|Signed, never on Refusal`) is the
clean shape (codex fix 2026-07-16). This is the ONLY spend-path CHANGE
permitted; do not alter any policy check, response shape, or the sign decision.
- **Keyed by `commitment_id`** (NOT bare unsigned-txid — codex/Fable fix
  2026-07-16: the same txid can have several live commitments with different
  expiry/user-signature instances; keying by txid would collide them). The
  record stores: `commitment_id`, the unsigned-txid (verified transaction
  identity — partials still bind to it), the canonical PSBT, per-input
  sighashes (recomputed by THIS node), the expected descriptor pubkey per
  (input, node_id), the spend's user-signature material, `user_sig_hash`
  (**tagged SHA-256 over the user's DER signature(s) + sighash-type byte(s),
  in input order, as this node verified them at ingress**), and the
  commitment expiry (its own, fixed eviction horizon — no extension).
  Registration reserves a candidate slot **after** the verdict. **In V0-8a, at
  capacity the candidate is simply NOT inserted** (log it; the `/sign` verdict
  and response are unchanged — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` refusal and
  no duress surface in this task). The full "capacity gate runs AFTER pin/safety
  so a duress arm/freeze is never suppressed" ordering is a **V0-4 obligation**
  (§ scope guard), because only V0-4 introduces the safety track that ordering
  protects.
Storage: `Arc<Mutex<PartialStore>>` on `Node` (the V0-8b Hold-expiry
timer task will read it too).
**Which verdicts register (decided 2026-07-16):** every NON-REFUSED verdict —
instantly-signed spends AND accepted-but-Pending hot spends, both at ingress
(V0-8b's Hold-expiry combine and Model B's sign-at-ingress require Pending
registration; a fast peer's partial arriving during our Hold then verifies
instead of bouncing as unknown-candidate). **Refused requests never
register** — nothing will ever combine for them, and refused junk must not
occupy the store. Escape candidates arrive with the tagged-request migration
(ADR-0013 §2) — out of V0-8a scope.

### 5. Partial-signature exchange (the core primitive)
The `partial` payload carries: `commitment_id`, `wallet_id`, the exact
unsigned-txid, input index, signer node id, sighash type, spend purpose,
`user_sig_hash`, and the partial signature (DER). (`protocol_version` is on the
envelope, not the payload.)
On receipt, after envelope authentication:
- **Equality checks:** payload `wallet_id` matches the envelope's;
  **`signer_node_id == sender_node_id`** (nodes only relay their own partials
  in V0-8a); the payload's txid matches the candidate's stored txid;
  `user_sig_hash` matches the registered candidate's.
- **Candidate check:** the `commitment_id` must be a **registered candidate**;
  a partial for an unknown commitment is answered `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`
  (retriable). The sender applies **bounded retry with backoff until the
  commitment expiry** — codex fix 2026-07-16: "re-sends at fire time" alone
  fails the escape-class immediate-fire case and races the concurrent fan-out,
  so an explicit bounded-retry rule (or a candidate-ready ack) is required, not
  an assumption. Do NOT hold unknown partials on the receiver.
- **`spend_purpose` is informational only** — nothing acts on it; transaction
  class is always derived locally (ADR-0012's node-derived class predicate).
- **Verify the partial** against the expected descriptor pubkey for
  (input, signer node id) over this node's **own registered sighash** before
  storing; import only verified signature fields into the canonical PSBT
  (**never blind-merge a peer PSBT**).
- **Structural store bound:** at most one partial per
  (candidate, input, signer); partials accepted only for registered
  candidates. No generic FIFO/LRU eviction — a compromised peer must not be
  able to evict quorum-useful partials.
- **Hard capacity cap (decided 2026-07-16, D12):** a configured maximum on
  active candidates AND total bytes, bounding RAM. **In V0-8a this gates ONLY
  the registry insertion, never the wire.** At capacity: the candidate is not
  inserted (log it), no live candidate is ever evicted (a compromised peer must
  not evict quorum-useful partials), and the `/sign` verdict/response is
  **unchanged** — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` message and no duress
  surface in this task. The insertion runs after the verdict, so the sign
  decision is never affected by store fullness.
  **V0-4 obligation (not built here):** once the duress safety track exists, the
  capacity check must run AFTER pin/safety so a duress SpendRequest still
  arms/freezes when the store is full (freeze + lockdown need no candidate slot;
  only the best-effort sweep candidate does) — preserving ADR-0012's "arming is
  keyed on the duress pin alone, unconditional, resource-independent." Recorded
  in the scope guard.
- **Eviction (decided 2026-07-16; simplified in re-review — D13):** a candidate
  and its stored partials are evicted together when the candidate's
  **commitment expires** (node's own clock). **Keyed by `commitment_id`; each
  distinct commitment is its own candidate — there is NO horizon extension**
  (a fresh commitment is a new key, a new candidate; the old one expires on its
  own clock). Pruning runs in the **same sweep the replay log already runs AND
  is enforced at `/channel` candidate lookup** (an idle node never runs the
  /sign-path sweep, so an expired candidate must be rejected on lookup too).
  **No armed/scheduled exemption in V0-8a** — V0-8a builds no arming, no timers,
  and no fire, so it can neither set nor clear such an exemption. The
  armed-candidate expiry exemption + its fire-complete cleanup are **V0-4/V0-8b
  work** (see scope guard), added where arming and firing actually live.
  *Tests: an expired candidate is gone after the sweep and a late partial for
  it is rejected as unknown/expired even with no intervening /sign; two live
  commitments over the same txid are two distinct candidates.*

### 6. Outbound: `send_partial` (reqwest)
- Add `reqwest` (default-tls off if unused; json feature as needed).
- `send_partial(peer, envelope)` POSTs to the peer's `/channel` with a
  per-send deadline and a bounded response read; a dead/unreachable peer is an
  error return, never a panic, and never blocks other sends (send to peers
  concurrently).
- **Partial-release authorization (ADR-0012):** `send_partial` is
  `pub(crate)`, with the invariant documented at its definition: no partial
  may leave the node before its candidate's authorized fire event; V0-8a has
  NO production caller — V0-8b must add the fire-authorization gate before
  wiring one. Tests are the only callers in this task.

### 7. Signing-oracle prohibition (structural, absolute)
A peer message must **never** cause the node to create a signature. The
`/channel` handler only *verifies and stores*; it has structurally no path to
invoke the signer. Add a test asserting no channel message of any `msg_type`
triggers signing.

### 8. DoS guards (layered)
- **Pre-auth (cheap, before any crypto):** the existing 1 MiB body limit; a
  global bound on concurrent `/channel` requests — so forged traffic cannot
  burn a victim peer's quota or the node's CPU unboundedly.
- **Post-auth (after envelope verification):** per-peer quota
  (envelopes/minute) keyed by authenticated sender_node_id; duplicate-envelope
  suppression (the nonce set); the structural PartialStore bound from §5.
- Isolated from the watchtower task.

### 9. Module docs
Give the channel module a module-level ASCII diagram of the envelope ingress
pipeline (protocol_version → recipient bind → manifest → endorsement → sig →
freshness → nonce → decode payload_b64 → equality → candidate(commitment_id) →
verify-partial → store, with every rejection exit).

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- **Derivation**: channel key is a pure function — same config ⇒ same channel
  pubkey; channel pubkey ≠ signing pubkey.
- **Manifest/startup invariants**: a config whose signing key is not in the
  descriptor fails startup; manifest hash is stable across field-order
  permutations of the input (canonicalization works); endorsement over the
  wrong manifest_hash rejected.
- **Identity/endorsement**: endorsed by an in-manifest signing key → accepted;
  endorsed by a non-member key → rejected; **an envelope carrying another
  vault's `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash` → rejected by the direct local-equality
  check, independently of endorsement validity** (a well-formed envelope for a
  different vault is refused before sender lookup); **an envelope signed by the
  coordinator auth key instead of an endorsed channel key → rejected** (the
  "coordinator cannot mint a node" property, executable).
- **Envelope ingress rejection branches** (each its own test): tampered
  `payload_b64` bytes (channel_sig fails) → rejected; **`recipient_node_id` ≠
  my node_id → rejected** (cross-recipient replay); **`protocol_version` ≠
  manifest's → rejected**; stale timestamp → rejected; **future-stamped
  envelope's nonce retained until its timestamp leaves the window** (no ~60s
  replay reopen); replayed nonce → rejected AND the nonce set is pruned by
  timestamp (bounded); oversized body → rejected; per-peer quota exceeded →
  rejected; global concurrent bound enforced; malformed JSON → 400;
  payload/envelope field mismatch → rejected; `signer_node_id != sender_node_id`
  → rejected.
- **Wire preimage**: signature verifies over the raw `payload_b64` ASCII bytes
  WITHOUT decoding first (a valid envelope authenticates before any
  base64-decode); a bit-flip in `payload_b64` fails verification.
- **Partial exchange**: a valid partial over a registered candidate + correct
  descriptor pubkey verifies and is stored; wrong signer key, wrong txid,
  wrong input index, wrong sighash, wrong `user_sig_hash` → rejected;
  unknown-`commitment_id` → `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE` (retriable); duplicate
  suppressed; a second different partial for the same (candidate, input,
  signer) does not evict the first verified one.
- **Registry lifecycle**: two live commitments over the same txid (fresh
  nonce/expiry) are distinct candidates (keyed by `commitment_id`), and
  registering the second does not evict the first; each expires on its own
  commitment clock (no horizon extension); an expired candidate is rejected at
  `/channel` lookup with no intervening `/sign` sweep; at the hard capacity cap
  the new candidate is **not inserted** and no live candidate is evicted,
  **and the `/sign` verdict/response is unchanged by the cap** (capacity gates
  the registry slot, not the sign decision — no wire `AT_CAPACITY` in V0-8a).
- **Signing-oracle**: no channel message of any `msg_type` causes the node to
  produce a signature (assert the signer is never invoked from the channel
  path).
- **Outbound**: `send_partial` to a dead peer returns an error — no panic, no
  partial leaked, other peers still receive theirs (concurrent sends).
- **Two in-process nodes, through the REAL path:** each node receives the
  spend via `POST /sign` (registering the candidate), then exchanges one
  verified partial via `/channel` over loopback axum — no test-only injection
  of candidates.
- `demo first-light` still exits 0 (additive task; the demo does not yet use
  the channel — V0-8b reworks the demo).

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, workspace `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` only.
  The ONLY `/sign`-path change is the `register_candidate` post-verdict funnel
  (§4) — a small behavior-preserving control-flow refactor, not literally one
  call site.
  Do NOT rework the coordinator or the demo (V0-8b). Do NOT build:
  combine/finalize/broadcast wiring (V0-8b), the duress state machine (V0-4),
  Tor or mTLS (v1), full manifest provisioning (V0-9), a
  leader/single-assembler (none is needed — the exchange is peer-to-peer),
  any session/connection state.
- **Explicit V0-8b/V0-4 obligations (recorded here so they are not lost):**
  (a) at ingress, refuse a hot-class spend whose commitment expiry < now +
  `hold_secs` + combine-slack (`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT`) — under
  combine-at-Hold-expiry such a spend can never legally fire and must die
  loudly, not become a zombie candidate (V0-8b). (b) **Armed-candidate expiry
  exemption + fire-complete cleanup** (V0-4/V0-8b): a candidate that is
  armed/scheduled-to-fire must be exempt from the commitment-expiry sweep AND
  the `/channel`-lookup expiry rejection until its fire completes (an
  escape-class duress `T = first_seen + duress_delay_secs` can exceed
  `max_commitment_age_secs`, so plain expiry would delete the residual escape
  before T and kill the Firing job); the exemption needs a finite lifecycle
  (cleared on fire-complete) so it cannot pin the capacity cap. This is
  deferred OUT of V0-8a (D13) because V0-8a builds no arming/timer/fire to set
  or clear it. (c) **Capacity gate AFTER pin/safety** — once the safety track
  exists, evaluate the candidate-store capacity check after arm/freeze so a
  duress SpendRequest is never dropped for fullness (V0-4). (d) **At-capacity
  on an accepted verdict is a zombie** — a Pending spend accepted but not
  registered (store full) can never combine in V0-8b; surface/refuse it loudly
  at ingress rather than silently, per the `EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` precedent
  (V0-8b/V0-4).
- Build the SIMPLEST correct thing that gives signed-envelope peer messaging +
  a verified partial exchange. Target ~1200–1600 lines including tests. If
  materially more, stop and simplify — but do not compress the wire contract
  or the rejection tests to hit the number.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.
